[PERSISTENT EXPERIENCE GUIDANCE]
## Consolidated Experience from Similar Tasks
Across cases, action failures came from unmet preconditions: forward movement failed when an obstacle (e.g., a stool) blocked the path; pickup failed when the object was not confirmed present, reachable, visible, or nearby; place failed when the robot was not holding the target object. General principle: never assume an action will succeed based solely on its intended effect. Before moving, inspect the path for obstacles and replan around them, remove them, or choose another route. Before pickup, confirm the target exists, is reachable, and is within the robot's current location or reach; if not, navigate to it or search for it. Before place, ensure the robot is actually holding the target object; if not, perform a successful pickup first. After each action, verify the predicted state rather than assuming success, and use any failure as a signal to replan.

## Preliminary Thinking
1) Identify the target object and destination. 2) Observe the environment and locate the target; verify it exists, is visible or reachable, and note potential obstacles. 3) Plan a path to the target and check for obstructions such as stools; if blocked, navigate around, remove the obstruction, or replan. 4) Navigate to the object. 5) Confirm the object is nearby and within reach before pickup; if not, adjust position or continue navigating. 6) Execute pickup and verify the robot is holding the object. 7) Plan and follow a path to the destination while checking for obstacles. 8) Execute place only if holding the object, then verify successful placement. Throughout, treat action outcomes as precondition checks and replan whenever movement, pickup, or place fails.
[/PERSISTENT EXPERIENCE GUIDANCE]
